assumptions: Onset at 15:14 was inferred by the investigating agent from per-minute metrics and log lines; it was not independently confirmed against an external clock or the flag provider's own event timestamp.

The alert record shows the incident as opening at 15:19:31 and closing at 15:20:02 (about 0.1 hours). That is the alert-to-mitigation window, not the customer-impact window — errors were already elevated for roughly five minutes before the alert fired, so any duration-based impact figure taken from the alert record understates it.

The defect at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32 was identified from error messages only. No one read the code or reproduced the division by zero during the incident; the diagnosis rests on the co-occurrence of the flag flip, the new stack trace, and the recovery on revert.

Whether the flag flip was a deliberate ramp, an operator mistake, or an automated change is not established. The flag provider's history showed one recent change; its author and intent were not recorded.
The pre-existing ~0-2% background of UpstreamTimeout errors on the account page is assumed to be unrelated normal noise. It was present before onset and was not investigated.
Impact is assumed to be limited to account-page requests, based on which log lines carried the new error. No per-endpoint or per-customer breakdown was gathered.
The mitigation is assumed durable only as long as the flag stays on. If the flag is ramped off again before the draft pull request lands, the same failure should be expected to recur.

The action log is internally inconsistent in ordering — the mitigation agent is shown reading flag history and reverting the flag at 15:19:50, at or before the timestamp at which it was called in, and the recorded action target is 'None' rather than the flag name. This is assumed to be a logging artifact rather than a second, unrecorded action.
input.executive_summary: A configuration switch in the online shop was turned off, which sent customers' account-page requests through a newer piece of code that contained an unnoticed defect. Those requests failed with an error instead of rendering the page. Failures began at 15:14 UTC on 16 September 2026 and were cleared by 15:20 UTC — roughly six minutes — affecting customers loading their account page during that window; checkout and other parts of the shop were not implicated. Automated response detected the problem, identified the switch as the trigger, turned it back on, and verified that the service returned to its normal error levels. A draft code fix for the underlying defect has been opened for human review and is not yet merged, so the switch is currently holding the problem shut rather than the defect being fixed.
input.root_cause: At 15:14:00Z the feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was flipped from on to off (partial at first — 109 off / 91 on in that minute, fully off from 15:15), which routed account-page requests away from the legacy fallback and onto the new spend-summary code path. That path contains a latent divide-by-zero, and requests hitting it failed with `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32`; per-minute error logs climbed from the ~0-2% background of upstream payment timeouts to 34% by 15:19. No deploy or release is recorded in the 24 hours before onset, so the flag change — not a code push — is what made the bug reachable. Restoring the flag to on returned the service to baseline, which confirms the causal link.
